# WikiKit — Full Documentation for LLMs

This single file contains the complete WikiKit documentation, inlined for LLM
consumption. A concise index is in `docs/llms.txt`.

WikiKit is a **headless, AI-native knowledge system for humans and agents**:
Markdown-first knowledge in, structured and agent-ready knowledge out. Sources
are archived verbatim, an LLM synthesizes maintained concept pages with
verifiable claims and citations, every change passes a human review gate as a
ChangeProposal, and the knowledge is reachable over HTTP/REST and MCP and
exportable as Markdown or OKF (Open Knowledge Format) bundles.

WikiKit's own operating and installation knowledge is an immutable built-in
system scope, shipped with the binary rather than seeded into a mutable user
space. Read it with `wikikit_guide`, `wikikit://system/agent-guide`, or
`GET /agent-guide.md`. User spaces remain reviewed, portable tenant data.

The guiding idea is curation over collection: WikiKit is not a dump of
everything you ever saw, it is a maintained set of concept pages an agent can
trust — every statement is a claim with a citation, a status and a lifecycle,
and nothing becomes visible without review. It is the knowledge foundation
that agents, dashboards and apps build on top of — WikiKit itself ships no CLI,
and its one human surface is the cockpit at `/cockpit` (§12), where the same
review gate applies: an edit there submits a change proposal like any other.

- Source: https://github.com/MikeBild/wikikit
- License: MIT

---

## 1. Core concept — the LLM-wiki loop

```
source (markdown | text | url)
  ──POST /v1/spaces/{space}/ingest──▶ archive verbatim (sha256 dedup)
  ──▶ classify (which concepts does this affect?)          [LLM, haiku]
  ──▶ synthesize new revision + claims + citations         [LLM, sonnet]
  ──▶ detect contradictions (declared-functional subject+predicate frames)
  ──▶ ONE pending ChangeProposal (staged rows, invisible to readers)
  ──▶ human reviews the structured diff and approves/rejects over REST
  ──▶ atomic apply: revision → current, claims → verified/disputed,
      space epoch bump, signed webhooks

question ──POST /v1/spaces/{space}/query──▶ grounded answer, kept as an Output
  ──▶ a human judges it worth keeping
  ──POST /v1/outputs/{id}/promote──▶ its markdown archived as a source marked
      derived_from_output_id ──▶ THE SAME pipeline above, ending in a proposal

scheduled briefing / health check ──▶ report history only; never a decision
  and never promotable
```

Key invariants:

- **Sources are never mutated.** The archived `raw_content` is the provenance
  anchor; `sha256(content)` makes re-ingesting the same document idempotent
  (`409 already_ingested`).
- **Proposed content is invisible by construction.** Search, concept reads and
  exports join through `current_revision_id` and visible claim statuses —
  staged rows cannot leak.
- **Every LLM call is audited.** Model, prompt version, input hash and token
  usage land in an agent-run ledger and in the `agent_meta` of every generated
  row — revision history answers "which model wrote this, from which source?".
- **An answer never becomes evidence on its own.** Answers are kept so they can
  be re-read, handed on and explicitly proposed as knowledge. Briefings and
  health checks remain reports and cannot be promoted.
  Filing good answers back without a human would leave the wiki quoting itself:
  every claim would still carry a verbatim quote from an archived document, and
  the document would be the wiki. Promotion is an explicit act, it runs the
  ordinary pipeline, and the source it creates is marked as derived so the
  `self-derived-only` lint rule can report a page that has ended up resting on
  nothing else.
- **Classification is a revisable claim, not a schema.** Relations and
  categorizations are claims with a source, a status and a lifecycle — they
  can be disputed and deprecated like any other statement.
- **Approval remains a human decision, now available over MCP.** Agents stage
  with ingest/propose; a principal with `knowledge:review` reads the complete
  diff — including every staged decision with its context, rationale and
  alternatives — through `wikikit_proposals`. The agent passes only the
  proposal id to `wikikit_review_proposal`; WikiKit then puts the decision in
  the human's hands through native MCP elicitation — the in-client form as the
  primary channel, with URL mode (the browser review page) as the fallback.

---

## 2. HTTP API

Base URL (self-host): `http://127.0.0.1:4060`. The live OpenAPI 3.1 document
is generated from the route registry and served at `/openapi.json` (committed
snapshot: `docs/openapi.json`). The `{space}` path segment is the space slug.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path                                          | Scope             | Purpose |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------|-------------------|---------|
| GET    | `/v1/spaces`                                  | knowledge:read    | List spaces visible to the current key |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces`                                  | admin             | Create a space (workspace scope for all knowledge) |
| GET    | `/v1/agent/briefing`                          | knowledge:read    | Compact, budgeted briefing for an ordered set of spaces |
| POST   | `/v1/agent/context`                           | knowledge:read    | Select task-relevant spaces from stable purpose metadata and return a compact briefing |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}`                          | knowledge:read    | Read a space (settings, epoch) |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/settings`                 | admin             | Merge or replace stable purpose metadata used for task-context selection |
| DELETE | `/v1/spaces/{space}`                          | admin             | Permanently delete a wiki and its dependent data after exact slug confirmation; refuses while ingest work is queued or running |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/charter`                  | knowledge:read    | Read the space charter — virtual document (authored markdown + derived overview); `?rev=N`; Accept: text/markdown renders it |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/charter/versions`         | knowledge:read    | List charter revisions (newest first) — the document version history |
| PUT    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/charter`                  | admin             | Write the charter (JSON `{markdown}` or raw text/markdown); authored text versions directly, an edited overview routes through the review gate |
| DELETE | `/v1/spaces/{space}/charter`                  | admin             | Delete the charter (supersede current revision; history retained). Idempotent |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/ingest`                   | knowledge:propose | Ingest a source (markdown\|text\|url) — async, `202` + `Location` to poll; `capture:true` parks it instead (`200 {status:"captured"}` — no LLM, no queue slot); `evidence:true` archives and indexes it as citable evidence only (done with `proposal_id` null, no model call) |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/ingest/document`        | knowledge:propose | Upload a document (pdf\|docx\|xlsx\|md\|txt\|csv, raw body) — extracted to Markdown then ingested |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/agent/sessions`           | knowledge:propose | Capture a coding-agent session: distil the rules a human taught — usually `no_learnings`, else one proposal; optional `session_id` makes repeated captures versions of ONE source stream |
| GET    | `/v1/ingests/{id}`                            | knowledge:propose | Ingest job status; done carries source_id and an optional proposal_id (null = no review work) |
| GET    | `/v1/ingests/{id}/triage`                     | knowledge:propose | Read the editable sorting suggestion stored with a captured item |
| POST   | `/v1/ingests/{id}/triage`                     | knowledge:propose | Generate and store an editable target, title, summary and confidence |
| POST   | `/v1/ingests/{id}/triage/resolve`             | knowledge:propose | Resolve one capture by processing, reusing an exact source, leaving it open or discarding it |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/ingests`                  | knowledge:read \| knowledge:propose | This space's ingest jobs newest-first — the inbox (`?status=queued\|running\|done\|failed\|quota_blocked\|captured\|discarded`, `?limit=`, `?cursor=`); rows are the same shape the single status read serves; captured rows carry `title` + `excerpt` |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/sources`                  | knowledge:read    | List archived sources (keyset pagination via `?before=`) |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/sources/{id}`             | knowledge:read    | Read one source (raw + normalized markdown) |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/sources/{id}/references`  | knowledge:read    | List current pages and pending proposals that use one archived source |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/sources/{id}/resynthesize` | knowledge:propose | Run the current pipeline over an immutable archived source and stage any result for human review |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/source-streams`           | knowledge:read    | List connector source streams (sync contract): head pointer, latest version, tombstone state |
| DELETE | `/v1/spaces/{space}/source-streams/{external_source_id}` | knowledge:propose | Tombstone a source stream (idempotent soft delete — the upstream document is gone) |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/decisions`                | knowledge:read    | List decisions (active/superseded), newest first — the decision log |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/decisions/{slug}`         | knowledge:read    | Read one decision: context, decision, rationale, rejected alternatives |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/concepts`                 | knowledge:read    | List concepts with an `evidence` summary per page, replaced by `not_measured` on a reference target (keyset `?after=`; ETag over the space epoch, 304 on If-None-Match) |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}`          | knowledge:read    | Read a concept: markdown + claims + citations + relations |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}/history`  | knowledge:read    | Revision history incl. agent_meta (model, prompt version, sources) |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}/neighbors` | knowledge:read   | The pages around this one: typed relations in BOTH directions (inbound = backlinks) plus same-space concepts quoting the same archived sources, ranked by shared-source count. LLM-free |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/deleted-concepts`         | knowledge:read    | List deleted concept tombstones for audit and restoration |
| DELETE | `/v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}`          | knowledge:propose | Stage page deletion for human review; history retained |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/concepts/{slug}/restore`  | knowledge:propose | Stage restoration of the last visible revision for review |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/search`                   | knowledge:read    | LLM-free full-text search; ranked hits with `<mark>` headlines, concept hits carrying the same `evidence` summary as the concept list. `?mode=approved_then_sources` appends the archived-source tier, and `?evidence_from=`/`?evidence_to=` (ISO instants, half-open) plus `?evidence_source_kind=meeting\|article\|note` narrow THAT tier only — approved hits are answered identically with the filters set. Hits carry `matched_via` (`lexical`/`vector`/`both`) when the hybrid ranker answered, and omit it otherwise |
| GET    | `/v1/search`                                  | knowledge:read    | The same ranked search across every wiki visible to the key; one query embedding is shared across the set and every hit names its origin wiki |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/query`                    | knowledge:read    | Grounded Q&A with inline citations (LLM; 503 without a key). Takes the same `evidence_*` filters as search, so an answer never leans on archived sources the list beside it excluded. The answer is kept as an output; the response additively carries `output_id` (null only if the row could not be written) |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/outputs`                  | knowledge:read    | What this wiki produced, newest-first: answers, scheduled briefings, health reports (`?kind=answer\|briefing\|health`, `?limit=`, `?cursor=`); rows carry the full markdown |
| GET    | `/v1/outputs/{id}`                            | knowledge:read    | Read one answer or scheduled report; `Accept: text/markdown` returns the complete stored document |
| POST   | `/v1/outputs/{id}/promote`                    | knowledge:propose | Propose an answer as knowledge: its markdown is archived as a source marked derived from the wiki itself and runs the ORDINARY pipeline → `202 {ingest_id}`. Briefing/health reports return 409 `output_not_promotable`. Idempotent — a second answer promotion returns the first job |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/health`                   | knowledge:read    | Composed maintenance report in one LLM-free read: lint findings + severity census (`?tier=quick\|deep`, default deep), coverage, the review queue with the age of its oldest change, the live ingest queue incl. parked thoughts. No verdict — the counts are the answer |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/attention`                | knowledge:read    | Human attention queue across proposals and inbox triage. Reports and read-only check findings are excluded |
| GET    | `/v1/audit`                                   | knowledge:read    | Append-only audit trail (audit.v1), newest first, filterable and cursor-paged |
| GET    | `/v1/attention`                               | knowledge:read    | Open human tasks across every visible wiki, globally oldest first |
| PUT    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/attention/{key}`          | knowledge:propose | Defer, discard or restore one queue item without changing its underlying knowledge object |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/schedules`                | admin             | The recurring briefing/health schedules of this space (at most one per kind) |
| PUT    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/schedules`                | admin             | Replace the COMPLETE schedule set (daily at HH:MM, or weekly on a weekday, in an IANA timezone). A kind left out is removed — hence no DELETE route. Idempotent |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/proposals`                | knowledge:read \| knowledge:review | List change proposals (`?status=pending`) |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/proposals`                | knowledge:propose | Stage a manual change proposal, incl. `relations_removed` (same review gate) |
| GET    | `/v1/proposals/{id}`                          | knowledge:read \| knowledge:review | Structured proposal diff incl. relations added/removed; `text/markdown` via Accept header |
| POST   | `/v1/proposals/{id}/approve`                  | knowledge:approve | Approve a pending proposal (atomic apply) |
| POST   | `/v1/proposals/{id}/reject`                   | knowledge:approve | Reject a pending proposal (staged rows kept for audit) |
| POST   | `/v1/proposals/{id}/split`                    | knowledge:review  | Split a pending proposal: full per-concept split, or defer a subset into one child |
| POST   | `/v1/proposals/{id}/request-changes`          | knowledge:review  | Terminal reject with a mandatory revision note — agents re-propose against the feedback |
| GET    | `/v1/proposals/{id}/lint`                     | knowledge:read    | Lint the STAGED content of one proposal (uncited claims, collisions, stale base, dangling links) |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/lint`                     | knowledge:read    | Knowledge health findings — LLM-free, CI-friendly; `?tier=quick` runs only the pulse rules, default `deep` runs everything |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/export`                   | knowledge:read    | Export the space as a zip bundle (`?format=md\|okf`) |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/import`                   | knowledge:propose | Import a bundle (zip): sources archived, knowledge staged as ONE proposal |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/webhooks`                 | admin             | List webhook endpoints |
| POST   | `/v1/spaces/{space}/webhooks`                 | admin             | Register a webhook endpoint (Standard Webhooks; secret shown once) |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` | admin             | Delivery attempts for one endpoint (status, attempts, backoff); newest first, `?limit=` up to 200 |
| GET    | `/v1/api-keys`                                | admin             | List visible API keys without plaintext or hashes |
| POST   | `/v1/api-keys`                                | admin             | Mint a scoped API key (plaintext shown once) |
| DELETE | `/v1/api-keys/{id}`                           | admin             | Revoke a DB-backed API key idempotently |
| GET    | `/v1/identities`                              | admin             | List SSO identity grants (scope ceiling, source, revocation) — never tokens or hashes |
| PUT    | `/v1/identities/{provider}/{subject}`         | admin             | Create/update an SSO identity grant (role XOR scopes; only `restore:true` clears a revocation; an omitted field is kept, `email: null` clears the stored address — but only until that identity's next SSO login mirrors the provider's asserted address back) |
| DELETE | `/v1/identities/{provider}/{subject}`         | admin             | Revoke an SSO identity grant: denies future logins AND kills its live OAuth tokens (idempotent) |
| GET    | `/v1/installation/knowledge-config`           | admin             | This installation's effective knowledge-shaping configuration, each value attributed as built-in or configured — never secrets |
| GET    | `/v1/stats/overview`                          | knowledge:read    | Cross-wiki overview: per visible space the actionable decision count, its oldest age and visible page count — plus server-side totals. Check findings are excluded. LLM-free, no verdict |
| GET    | `/v1/stats/mcp`                               | admin             | Global privacy-safe MCP session, protocol and tool usage |
| GET    | `/v1/stats/llm`                               | admin             | Global measured LLM tokens, configured cost, cache use and explicit unpriced usage, with per-space totals |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/stats/http`              | knowledge:read    | HTTP calls, outcomes, latency/size and exact-window adoption |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/stats/usage`             | knowledge:read    | Cross-transport search/read/query/ingest/proposal behavior |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/stats/coverage`          | knowledge:read    | Coverage insights: disputed claims, review latency, freshness, read/link hubs, gap topics |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/stats/reviews`           | knowledge:read    | Cross-transport proposal inspection and review behavior |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/stats/ingests`           | knowledge:read    | Time-bucketed ingest lifecycle and duration aggregates |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/stats/knowledge`         | knowledge:read    | Time-bucketed knowledge growth and review activity |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/stats/llm`               | knowledge:read    | Time-bucketed measured LLM calls, tokens, configured USD cost, cache ratio and explicit unpriced usage |
| GET    | `/v1/spaces/{space}/stats/webhooks`          | knowledge:read    | Time-bucketed webhook events and outcomes |
| GET    | `/health`                                     | public            | Liveness — `200 "ok"` while the process is up |
| GET    | `/ready`                                      | public            | Readiness — `{status, version}`; 503 while draining |
| GET    | `/metrics`                                    | public            | Prometheus metrics |
| GET    | `/.well-known/service-descriptor.json`        | public            | Version + a sha256 per self-description artifact, so a watcher can tell "unchanged" from "changed" in one small GET |
| GET    | `/openapi.json`                               | public            | Generated OpenAPI 3.1 spec |
| GET    | `/review/{id}`                                | public            | Human review page for one proposal (content-free shell; data loads with the reviewer's key) |
| GET    | `/agent-guide.md`                             | public            | Built-in agent operating and no-CLI client setup guide |
| GET    | `/llms.txt`                                   | public            | Documentation index (llmstxt.org format) |
| GET    | `/llms-full.txt`                              | public            | This file |
| GET    | `/.well-known/llms.txt`                       | public            | Well-known alias of `/llms.txt` |
| GET    | `/.well-known/llms-full.txt`                  | public            | Well-known alias of `/llms-full.txt` |
| GET    | `/install.sh`                                 | public            | Agent hooks installer (macOS/Linux) — `curl -fsSL <host>/install.sh \| sh` wires Claude Code, Codex and Cursor |
| GET    | `/install.ps1`                                | public            | Agent hooks installer (Windows, PowerShell 5.1) — `irm <host>/install.ps1 \| iex` |
| GET    | `/install/hooks/{script}`                     | public            | One lifecycle hook script (closed set of six: briefing/context/capture as `.sh` and `.ps1`) |

MCP (Streamable HTTP) is mounted at POST /mcp — intentionally outside the
REST/OpenAPI surface. Local clients use scoped API keys; remote MCP clients
use OAuth 2.1 discovery, PKCE and explicitly requested scopes (§7).

The stats resources are product-owned analytics, not a consumer-specific
reporting interface. The original ingests/knowledge/LLM/webhook readers derive
operational and growth metrics from durable product tables. The opt-in usage
ledger additionally measures actual HTTP and MCP connections/calls plus
search/read/query/ingest/proposal/review behavior. Space readers reuse normal
space-aware `knowledge:read`; global MCP aggregation requires `admin`.

All usage responses use schema `wikikit.usage-stats.v1`. Query parameters are
`bucket=hour|day|month|year`, RFC3339 `from`/`to`, `tz=UTC`,
`traffic_class=organic|synthetic|internal|all`, and at most two comma-separated
surface-specific `group_by` dimensions. Totals run a separate full-window SQL
query, so unique actors/sessions and percentiles are exact instead of sums of
buckets. Metric values declare `value_kind`, `value_state`, sample size and,
for ratios, numerator/denominator. `quality` declares `sampled:false`, exact
unique counting, retention/dropped events and `content_captured:false`.
Outcome `no_answer` (with `no_answer`/`no_answer_ratio` metrics) counts
query calls the knowledge base honestly answered with "not covered" — the
demand-vs-coverage signal; it appears on the knowledge surface only.

Collection is off by default. Enable `WIKIKIT_USAGE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` only
with an independent `WIKIKIT_USAGE_HMAC_SECRET`. Stored events contain
controlled operation/route/tool names, outcome/status, traffic/source,
duration/size/count/capacity and product-local HMAC actor/session ids. They
never contain content, prompts, search/question text, MCP arguments/results,
raw paths/query strings, IP/UA, credentials, e-mail, space slugs or dynamic
resource ids. Anonymous HTTP is never fingerprinted; health/docs/stats traffic
is internal; raw rows expire after `WIKIKIT_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS`. Cross-product
actor joins are forbidden. Use `/v1/spaces/{space}/lint` for current data quality.

### Conventions

- **Request IDs:** every response carries a 12-hex `x-request-id` header; the
  same id appears in error envelopes and logs.
- **Trace context:** valid W3C `traceparent` trace ids are continued with a new
  server span; every response and structured request log carries `trace_id`,
  `span_id` and `parent_span_id`.
- **Pagination is keyset:** `?limit=&after=` (opaque cursor); responses carry
  `next_after: string | null` (sources paginate backwards with `?before=` and
  `next_before`; the inbox and the output archive walk the same direction and
  spell the parameter `?cursor=`, answering `next_before`).
- **Caching:** concept lists carry `ETag: "<space-epoch>"`; the epoch bumps on
  every approved proposal, so `If-None-Match` gives cheap 304s on any read of
  approved knowledge.
- **Evidence in the concept list and on search hits:** items of `GET .../concepts` carry
  `evidence: {claims, uncited_claims, sources}` — how many claims the page
  makes, how many of those cite nothing, and how many distinct sources back it.
  Only visible claims count (`verified|disputed|deprecated`); `proposed` and
  `draft` claims belong to a pending proposal, not to knowledge, and are never
  counted — an unreviewed proposal must not make a page look evidenced.
  This is what lets an agent decide **which page to read before reading it**:
  ask for the list, then spend the fetch on a page whose claims are cited by
  sources rather than on one that asserts more than it can show. Read
  `uncited_claims` against `claims`, not on its own, and treat `sources` as
  breadth — one source usually backs several claims, so it is not
  `claims - uncited_claims`. `claims: 0` is a page a human wrote by hand
  without sources: a real state of published knowledge, not an error and not a
  missing field. The counts describe the page as it stands now — claims hang
  off the concept, not off a revision, so they do not move with `rev`.
  `GET .../search` serves the same object on a `kind: "concept"` hit, from the
  same aggregate over the same visible claims, so the numbers agree with the
  list for the same page and the choice of which result to open is as informed
  as the choice of which row to open. `kind: "claim"` and `kind: "source_chunk"`
  hits deliberately carry no `evidence`: the page's totals do not answer whether
  the matched claim itself is quoted, and a source-evidence hit is unreviewed
  archive material — giving it an evidence summary would advertise it as
  approved knowledge, which is exactly what its tier says it is not.
  The object is also absent — on the list and on a concept hit alike — for a
  REFERENCE TARGET: a page an import created so that reviewed relations had
  somewhere to land, whose own body says the knowledge lives on the pages it
  points at. There is nothing there to evidence, and three zeros would read as
  the finding that a knowledge page rests on nothing. Absence therefore never
  means zero: where the three numbers are served they are measured, and where
  they are missing the question did not apply.
  The absence says so itself rather than leaving a hole: in place of `evidence`
  such a row carries `not_measured: {reason: "reference_target"}`, and — only
  where the page nevertheless holds visible claims — a `withheld_claims` count,
  which is the number `evidence.claims` would have carried, from the same
  aggregate. It is absent, never `0`, when there is nothing to withhold. It is
  not the measurement renamed (there is no `uncited_claims` and no `sources`
  here, and never will be) and it is not a finding (no severity, no advice — the
  `scaffolded-claims` lint rule owns that judgement). A readable row carries
  `evidence` or `not_measured`, never both and never neither, so a client never
  has to deduce which kind of nothing it is holding from the rows around it. A
  concept hit carrying neither is a page that stopped being readable between the
  ranking and the count. A reference target is recognised
  by the `kind` its current revision carries: WikiKit's own
  `structural-reference` always, plus whatever markers the installation declares
  in `WIKIKIT_SCAFFOLDING_KINDS` (§11) — a fact about one deployment's import
  history, so it is read from the environment rather than known by the product.
  Two installations may therefore withhold `evidence` on different rows; what
  never varies is what an absence means. Which markers a given installation
  honours is reportable by that installation:
  `GET /v1/installation/knowledge-config` (admin) returns them in the order the
  reads apply them, each attributed `built_in` (WikiKit's own, not configurable
  away) or `configured` (the operator wrote it). WikiKit ships no
  deployment-specific default, so anything not built in was declared by that
  installation.
  Nothing else is needed to interpret an absence — the meaning is fixed by the
  contract — but it answers WHY a particular row has none.
- **Narrowing the archived tier:** with `mode=approved_then_sources`, three
  optional parameters narrow the `source_evidence` hits and nothing else:
  `evidence_from`/`evidence_to` (ISO instants with offset, half-open, over when
  a source was ARCHIVED) and `evidence_source_kind` (`meeting|article|note`).
  Approved hits are answered identically with them set — the two tiers share no
  clock (a page is dated by its review, a source by its arrival) and no kind
  alphabet, and a curated page does not become untrue because it is old. The
  filters do not switch the tier on: without the mode they are inert. Two
  limits worth knowing before relying on them: a source carries `source_kind`
  only where the ingesting client declared one, so `evidence_source_kind=note`
  drops every source that never named itself — most connector-fed material
  among them, which makes this an exclusion rather than a classification; and
  there is no `report` value, so "machine-fed, not hand-filed" is not
  expressible here at all. `POST .../query` takes the same three, so a grounded
  answer never leans on archive a narrowed search excluded.
- **Async ingest:** `POST .../ingest` answers `202` with
  `{ingest_id, status:"queued"}` and `Location: /v1/ingests/{id}`; poll until
  `done` (carries `source_id`; `proposal_id` is nullable when no affected or new
  knowledge requires review) or `failed` (carries `error.code/message`).
- **Capture:** the same route with `capture:true` PARKS the content instead —
  `200 {ingest_id, status:"captured"}`, no LLM call, no dedup pre-check, and no
  slot under the per-space queue ceiling. A captured row is invisible to the
  worker until `POST /v1/ingests/{id}/triage/resolve` records the human choice.
  Processing pays the LLM guard and queue-room check at that moment; discarding
  is terminal and the row stays for the record. Identical text parked twice is
  two captured rows: dedup is
  content-hash-on-archive, and a capture archives nothing yet.
- **Evidence:** the same route with `evidence:true` runs acquire → archive →
  chunk and completes `done` with `proposal_id` null BEFORE classify ever
  runs — zero model calls, zero review work. The source is immediately
  searchable in the `source_evidence` tier and citable by `chunk_id` later.
  Unlike capture it does real worker work, so the dedup pre-check, the queue
  ceiling and the sync contract (`external_source_id`/`source_version`)
  apply unchanged; like capture it works keyless. `evidence` excludes
  `capture` and `resynthesize` (400 on either combination).

### Examples

Ingest a note and poll:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/spaces/default/ingest" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"markdown":"# OKF\nOKF is a draft spec for knowledge bundles.","title":"OKF note","source_kind":"note"}'
# → 202 {"ingest_id":"...","status":"queued"}  + Location: /v1/ingests/{id}

curl -s "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/ingests/<id>" -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..."
# → {"ingest_id":"...","status":"done","proposal_id":"...","source_id":"...","error":null}
```

Review the diff (human-readable) and approve:

```bash
curl -s "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/proposals/<id>" -H "Accept: text/markdown" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..."          # chat-readable structured diff

curl -s -X POST "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/proposals/<id>/approve" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"note":"source is current"}'
```

Search (LLM-free) vs. query (LLM synthesis with citations):

```bash
curl -s "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/spaces/default/search?q=okf" -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..."
curl -s -X POST "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/spaces/default/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"question":"Is OKF production ready?"}'
```

Keep a good answer — the loop's second half. `/query` returns `output_id`;
promoting it stages a change somebody still has to approve:

```bash
OUT=$(curl -s -X POST "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/spaces/default/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"question":"Is OKF production ready?"}' | jq -r .output_id)

curl -s "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/outputs/$OUT" -H "Accept: text/markdown" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..."   # exactly what promotion would archive

curl -s -X POST "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/outputs/$OUT/promote" -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..."
# → 202 {"ingest_id":"..."} + Location: /v1/ingests/{id}   — poll it like any ingest
```

Lint as a CI gate:

```bash
curl -s "$WIKIKIT_URL/v1/spaces/default/lint" -H "Authorization: Bearer wk_..." \
  | jq -e '[.findings[] | select(.severity=="error")] | length == 0'
```

---

## 3. Authentication & scopes

API keys look like `wk_<43 chars base64url>`; the plaintext is returned exactly
once by `POST /v1/api-keys` and stored only as an HMAC-SHA256 hash keyed with
`WIKIKIT_KEY_PEPPER`. Send a key as `Authorization: Bearer wk_...` or
`X-API-Key: wk_...`.

Scopes:

| Scope               | Grants |
|---------------------|--------|
| `knowledge:read`    | spaces, sources, concepts, history, search, query, proposals (read), lint, export |
| `knowledge:propose` | ingest + ingest status, manual proposals, import |
| `knowledge:review` | inspect proposals (REST GET proposals too) and start the MCP review where the human decides (implied by `knowledge:approve`) |
| `knowledge:approve` | approve/reject proposals over REST — the human-operator review credential; implies `knowledge:review` |
| `admin`             | spaces (create), webhooks, api-keys; implies all knowledge scopes |
| `*`                 | bootstrap key — everything |

Keys can be **space-scoped**: a key bound to one space gets
`403 insufficient_scope` on any other space. Two distinct failure modes:
`401 unauthorized` = the key was not recognized (missing/revoked/wrong pepper);
`403 insufficient_scope` = recognized key, missing scope or wrong space.

In dev, when no admin key exists at boot, a bootstrap key with scope `*` is
generated and printed **once** to stdout (pin it via
`WIKIKIT_BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY`). Recommended production key split: a read key for
consumers, a propose key for agents, an approve key for reviewers — never hand
the approve scope to an autonomous agent.

### The cockpit's credential plane

The cockpit (§12) is a browser, and a browser cannot hold an API key safely — a
token that reaches JavaScript is a token any script on the page can read. So it
uses the OAuth mount's browser operator session instead, over three endpoints
that live outside the ROUTES registry for the same reason `/mcp` does:

| | |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/session` | `{"session": {name, kind, scopes, space_id, provider_id}}` or `{"session": null}`. **Never 401** — an anonymous tab is an answer, not a failure. |
| `GET /v1/identity/cockpit-login?return_to=…` | Enters the same provider chooser every other sign-in uses. `return_to` must be a same-origin path under `/cockpit`; anything else falls back to `/cockpit/`. |
| `DELETE /v1/session` | Revokes the session. Requires a same-origin `Origin` header. |

The console is deliberately **not** an OAuth client: consent exists so a third
party can be told what it is about to be granted, and an installation's own
console is not a third party. Its login state carries `purpose = 'cockpit'` and
a return address, and a CHECK constraint makes that shape mutually exclusive
with an authorization request's.

The resulting cookie (HttpOnly, `SameSite=Lax`, `__Host-` prefixed under https)
is a **fallback** credential on `/v1`: it is consulted only when a request
carries neither `Authorization` nor `X-API-Key`, so no API-key client's 401 or
403 changes shape. Unsafe methods additionally require a same-origin `Origin` —
`SameSite=Lax` does not cover them all, and a CSRF token would have to reach
JavaScript, which is what the cookie was chosen to avoid. Scopes are re-cut
against the live identity grant on every read, so narrowing a grant narrows
every session it minted.

---

## 4. Domain model

| Entity | What it is |
|--------|------------|
| Space | Workspace scope; carries `settings` (incl. the controlled predicate vocabulary) and an `epoch` that bumps on every approved proposal |
| Source | An archived original document (`markdown\|text\|url\|import`), verbatim + normalized markdown, `sha256` content hash = idempotency anchor |
| Concept | A wiki page identity (slug) whose content lives in immutable revisions; `current_revision_id` points at the approved one |
| Revision | Immutable page version: `proposed → current → superseded` (or `rejected`); carries `agent_meta` `{model, prompt_version, input_hash, usage, source_ids}` |
| Claim | A verifiable statement `subject / predicate / object` with `confidence`, citations, and status `proposed → verified → disputed → deprecated` |
| Citation | Claim provenance: source + verbatim quote + locator |
| Relation | Concept link: `related \| part_of \| depends_on \| contradicts \| supersedes`; added via `concepts[].relations`, removed via a proposal's top-level `relations_removed` (approval deactivates the edge, soft delete) |
| Decision | A first-class recorded decision: context, decision, rationale, alternatives (the decision-log pattern; meeting sources are mined for these) |
| ChangeProposal | The review gate: staged rows in the target tables (never a JSON diff blob) that flip atomically on approve |
| Ingest job | Async pipeline run: `queued → running → done\|failed\|quota_blocked` |
| Agent run | LLM audit ledger entry: kind, model, prompt_version, input_hash, usage, duration |
| Output | Something the base PRODUCED: an answer (`/query`), a scheduled `briefing` or a `health` report. A derived artifact — never knowledge, never evidence, never read by synthesis. Promotion archives its markdown as an ordinary source and stages an ordinary proposal |
| Schedule | At most one `briefing` and one `health` entry per space: daily at HH:MM, or weekly on a weekday, in an IANA timezone — a closed set, deliberately not a cron expression |

Contradiction handling is deterministic and cardinality-aware: only predicates
listed in a space's `settings.functional_predicates` treat different objects
for the same `(subject, predicate)` as a conflict. Undeclared predicates are
multi-valued. On a declared-functional collision both sides flip to `disputed`
and a `contradicts` relation is ensured.

Stale-base protection: every proposed revision remembers the revision it was
synthesized against; approving a proposal whose base is no longer current
fails with `409 stale_base` instead of clobbering newer knowledge.

Supersede-retire: when a source stream's new version supersedes the previous
head, proposals still pending on that predecessor flip to terminal `failed`
with a review note naming the newer source, the moment the replacement is
staged. The head is current truth, so those proposals could only ever have
been burned on `stale_base` at review time. Approved, rejected, failed and
split proposals are never touched.

---

## 5. Ingest pipeline & LLM usage

```
acquire → archive → dedup-gate → classify → synthesize (per concept)
        → contradiction-detect → propose (one transaction) → webhook
```

- **Acquire:** markdown/text in the request body, or `{url}` (HTML is
  normalized to Markdown; raw archived verbatim). An optional `source_kind`
  (`meeting | article | note`) is recorded on the source and steers synthesis —
  `meeting` turns on decision mining.
- **Classify** (`WIKIKIT_MODEL_CLASSIFY`, default `claude-haiku-4-5`): one call
  with the source + a compact concept index → which existing concepts are
  affected, which new concepts are warranted.
- **Synthesize** (`WIKIKIT_MODEL_SYNTHESIS`, default `claude-sonnet-5`): one
  call per affected concept — current revision + source → new markdown,
  summary, claims with quotes and confidences, relations, and (for `meeting`
  sources) explicit decisions staged as proposed `wk_decisions`. Categorizations
  are emitted as claims, not fixed taxonomy, so a later source can dispute them.
  Prompts are versioned (`synthesize.v1`); a shipped prompt change adds a new
  version.
- **Answer** (`WIKIKIT_MODEL_ANSWER`, default `claude-sonnet-5`): grounded Q&A
  for `POST .../query` — answers only from retrieved evidence, cites inline,
  flags disputed claims, and says "not in the knowledge base" on empty
  retrieval instead of hallucinating.

The LLM runs through the Vercel AI SDK; the provider is config-selected
(`WIKIKIT_LLM_PROVIDER` = `anthropic` (default) / `openai` / `google`) and only
its API key has no default. Switching provider also means setting the three
`WIKIKIT_MODEL_*` variables, whose defaults are Anthropic model ids that other
providers 404 on — config refuses to boot when a model id recognisably belongs
to a provider other than the selected one, naming the setting, both providers
and the repair, while an id of unrecognised shape is allowed through so a model
newer than the binary can never block a start. The structured-output JSON schema is WikiKit's own, shaped to
the strictest provider: every property key appears in `required`, with optional
ones nullable so a model can decline a field instead of inventing one. Without
a key every LLM-free feature (search, read, history, lint, export, import,
review) keeps working; ingest and query answer `503 llm_not_configured` with
actionable hints. Anthropic prompt caching is
wired (the static system prompt is a cache-controlled prefix), so repeated
synthesis pays for the cached prefix at ~0.1x. `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is honored
for the anthropic provider (test stubs).

---

## 6. Error envelope

Every non-2xx JSON response (and every MCP tool error) is a terminal,
actionable envelope — never a bare string:

```json
{
  "error": "human-readable message",
  "code": "machine_code",
  "request_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
  "next_best_actions": ["optional short imperative hints"]
}
```

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|------|------|---------|
| `bad_request` | 400 | request failed schema validation (zod details in `error`) |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | missing, unknown or revoked API key |
| `insufficient_scope` | 403 | known key, missing scope or wrong space |
| `not_found` | 404 | resource does not exist |
| `already_ingested` | 409 | content-hash hit; envelope carries `source_id` |
| `proposal_not_pending` | 409 | proposal already reviewed |
| `stale_base` | 409 | concept changed since the proposal was synthesized |
| `approval_requires_human` | 400 | `decision`/`note` passed as review tool input; the decision belongs to the human; proposal is unchanged |
| `elicitation_not_supported` | 409 | form capability vanished mid-review (backstop; the tool normally returns a `human_review_required` hand-off first); proposal is unchanged |
| `invalid_elicitation_response` | 400 | human form remained invalid after one bounded retry; proposal is unchanged |
| `elicitation_timeout` | 408 | human form timed out; proposal is unchanged |
| `elicitation_failed` | 502 | client or transport failed before a valid human decision; proposal is unchanged |
| `body_too_large` | 413 | body exceeds `WIKIKIT_MAX_BODY_BYTES` |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | slow down |
| `ingest_not_captured` | 409 | triage resolution on a job that is not parked in `captured` |
| `ingest_queue_full` | 429 | this space already has `WIKIKIT_INGEST_MAX_QUEUED_PER_SPACE` jobs waiting; envelope carries `queued` and `limit`, and nothing was queued. NOT a rate limit: the pacing was fine, the work queue is full — let it drain or clear the review backlog holding it up, do not retry in a loop |
| `internal_error` | 500 | unexpected failure (message never leaks internals) |
| `llm_not_configured` | 503 | set the key for the configured `WIKIKIT_LLM_PROVIDER` to enable ingest/query (the error names it) |
| `draining` | 503 | graceful shutdown in progress |

---

## 7. MCP server

Streamable HTTP at `POST /mcp` (plus GET/DELETE for SSE/session close), built
on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`. Local/operator clients use the same `wk_` key
auth as REST. Remote interactive clients use OAuth 2.1 discovery, DCR,
authorization code + PKCE, rotating refresh tokens and Bearer access tokens.
An unauthenticated `/mcp` response advertises protected-resource metadata via
`WWW-Authenticate`; OAuth tokens expose only the consented read/propose/approve
scopes, capped by the configured identity-provider policy.

Remote human login is configured only by the provider-neutral
`WIKIKIT_OAUTH_PROVIDERS` JSON list. It accepts one API-key plus multiple named
direct OIDC adapters concurrently; product names are configuration values.
WikiKit owns each OIDC client, callback, secret and policy; no cross-product
authentication runtime is involved. Each OIDC adapter requires the immutable
`sub` claim and applies an explicit exact-subject or provider-verified-email
allow-list. Email is optional and unverified email is ignored. The stored
address is a mirror, not an operator field: every SSO callback for an existing
row writes back whatever the provider asserts, so `PUT ... {"email": null}`
clears it only until that identity signs in again. Erasure that lasts comes
from the identity no longer signing in — clear the address and THEN revoke the
grant (a revoked row denies login, and the order matters because `PUT` on a
revoked grant is 409 without `restore:true`, which would un-revoke it) — or
from removing the person at the identity provider. The interactive permission ceiling
defaults to `knowledge:read,knowledge:propose`; add `knowledge:review` for
review-starting agents and `knowledge:approve` only
for trusted human reviewers, and the client must request it explicitly. OAuth
never issues `admin`. A connector stores the tools and scopes it scanned, so a
new tool or scope requires a rescan/reconnect rather than silently broadening
an old token.

The browser chooser implements `mcp-auth-v2` and always renders `Continue with
SSO` before `Continue with API key`; configured labels never change those
actions. Authorize redirects through the generic
`/v1/identity/login/start?login_state=<opaque>` funnel. Provider discovery is
`GET /v1/identity/providers`; assertion exchange is
`POST /v1/identity/sessions` with `{provider_id,identity_token}` and the exact
response `{api_key,principal_id,context_id,email}`; `email` is nullable and
contains only a provider-verified address. Only the generic
start/callback/logout routes exist—there are no provider-named or legacy
aliases. WikiKit returns `context_id:null` and keeps space authorization in the
issued key.

Sessions are leases: idle TTL sweep (`WIKIKIT_MCP_SESSION_TTL_MS`), hard cap
(`WIKIKIT_MCP_MAX_SESSIONS`) with oldest-idle eviction; a different key on a
known session id gets 404 (hijack guard); an unknown session id gets JSON-RPC
`-32001` so clients re-initialize cleanly. Origin headers are validated
(DNS-rebinding guard) and `mcp-protocol-version` is checked against the SDK's
supported versions.

**Scope-gating = tool visibility**: `tools/list` returns only tools whose
scope the key holds — a `knowledge:read` key sees only the read tools.
`wikikit_proposals` and `wikikit_review_proposal` require `knowledge:review`
(implied by `knowledge:approve`); the REST approve/reject endpoints still
demand `knowledge:approve`, so a review-scoped agent key can never approve
over HTTP. The review tool accepts only `{proposal_id}` — passing
`decision` or `note` as arguments is refused with `approval_requires_human`
before anything else happens.

On a client advertising `capabilities.elicitation.form` — the primary channel;
in a terminal client this is the in-terminal review dialog — the tool issues a
native `elicitation/create` form for the human-owned decision and optional
note. Accepted forms perform the atomic write and persist
`review_channel:"mcp_elicitation"`; decline, cancel, timeout, invalid data or
transport failure performs no mutation. A cancel arriving faster than a human
could read the form (the client advertised the capability but never rendered
it) falls back — to URL mode if advertised, else to the
`human_review_required` hand-off below — instead of being reported as a human
cancel. The POST response stays on the event-stream transport so the server
can originate the elicitation request while the tool call is in flight.

On a client advertising `capabilities.elicitation.url` (MCP 2025-11-25) whose
form is unavailable or provably unrendered, the tool falls back to URL mode:
it issues `elicitation/create` with `mode:"url"`, an `elicitationId` and the
review-page URL (`GET /review/{id}?via=elicitation`). Accepting is consent to
open the page, nothing more — the tool returns
`{proposal_id, status:"pending", outcome:"url_review_started", review_url,
mutation_applied:false, poll_with:"wikikit_proposals", agent_instructions}`
immediately, and the human decides on the page with their own reviewer key.
That review is audited as `review_channel:"url_elicitation"`, and the server
sends `notifications/elicitation/complete` with the `elicitationId` on the
originating session (best-effort — polling `wikikit_proposals` remains the
durable path). Declining or cancelling the consent performs no mutation and
still returns the `review_url`.

On a client without any elicitation capability the tool performs no
mutation and returns a hand-off instead of an error:
`{proposal_id, status:"pending", outcome:"human_review_required",
review_url, mutation_applied:false, poll_with:"wikikit_proposals",
agent_instructions}`. The `agent_instructions` are scope-matched. A
review-scoped key hands the user the `review_url` — the embedded review page
at `GET /review/{id}`, where the human authenticates with their own reviewer
key and decides — and polls `wikikit_proposals`; it never collects
approve/reject in chat and never calls the REST review endpoints on the
human's behalf. A key the operator deliberately granted `knowledge:approve`
is additionally instructed that it may execute the user's clearly stated
approve/reject instruction over REST, quoting it in the audit note.

Form elicitation is synchronous and bounded by
`WIKIKIT_MCP_ELICITATION_TIMEOUT_MS`; the URL-mode consent uses the same
bound, but the review itself is out of band and unbounded. The pending
proposal is already the durable workflow object, so WikiKit deliberately adds
no MCP task or dialog lease. A reviewer can retry later.

**Coding-agent loop** (`docs/coding-agent-integration.md`): an optional
SessionStart hook injects only a compact briefing, and UserPromptSubmit selects
task-relevant additional spaces from stable space-purpose metadata. A
SessionEnd/Stop hook
posts the transcript to `POST /v1/spaces/{space}/agent/sessions`, which distils
ONLY durable rules a human explicitly taught and stages them as a proposal.
A routine session answers `no_learnings` and writes nothing; the transcript is
distilled and dropped, never archived. Those hooks fire on every turn-end their
host offers, posting the same transcript grown longer each time, so the body
carries an optional `session_id`: captures sharing one become versions of a
single source stream keyed `agent-session:<session_id>` (supersedes chain, one
head), a re-capture whose learnings did not change answers `already_captured`,
and the predecessor's still-pending proposal is retired the moment the newer
one is staged. No `source_version` is sent — content-hash dedup decides
sameness, and distillation is not deterministic enough for a transcript-derived
marker. Captures without a `session_id` behave exactly as before. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor expose
equivalent lifecycle events; example hook scripts ship as `.sh`/`.ps1` pairs
(`examples/agent-hooks/`, scripts `wikikit-briefing`/`wikikit-context`/
`wikikit-capture`) and every server serves its own agent hooks installer at
`GET /install.sh` (macOS/Linux) and `GET /install.ps1` (Windows) — unrelated
to the repository's git pre-push `hooks:install`.

**Self-description**: `initialize` returns `instructions` (how the tools fit
together; the staging-not-publishing rule), and the server advertises a
`resources` capability. `wikikit_guide` exposes the compact system guide even
to tools-only clients. `resources/list` offers the same guide at
`wikikit://system/agent-guide` plus this documentation at
`wikikit://docs/llms.txt` and `wikikit://docs/llms-full.txt`, readable via
`resources/read`, so an MCP-only client never needs an HTTP GET to learn the
API. Resources are not scope-gated; the same files are public over HTTP.

### Tools

| Tool | Scope | Behavior | readOnly | destructive | idempotent | openWorld |
|------|-------|----------|----------|-------------|------------|-----------|
| `wikikit_guide` | knowledge:read | Read code-versioned system knowledge and no-CLI client setup; no database seed | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_spaces` | knowledge:read | Discover spaces visible to the current key | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_briefing` | knowledge:read | Compact budgeted orientation for an ordered set of spaces | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_context` | knowledge:read | Select relevant spaces from the current task, or honor an explicit manual space list | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_search` | knowledge:read | Ranked FTS hits (raw evidence, no synthesis); `mode`, `include_imports` and the three `evidence_*` filters mirror the REST query | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_read` | knowledge:read | Full concept: markdown + claims + citations + relations + rev | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_sources` | knowledge:read | Provenance chain down to original sources (by concept slug or source_id) | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_decisions` | knowledge:read | Decision log: one decision by slug, or list all active/superseded | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_history` | knowledge:read | Revisions incl. agent_meta (model, prompt version) | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_lint` | knowledge:read | Knowledge health findings; `tier:'quick'` runs only the pulse rules, default `'deep'` everything | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_health` | knowledge:read | One LLM-free read of how a wiki is doing: every lint finding with a severity census (`tier` as in `wikikit_lint`), the coverage block, the review queue WITH the age of its oldest change, and the live ingest queue incl. parked thoughts. Reports numbers, never a verdict | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_overview` | knowledge:read | One LLM-free read across every visible wiki: proposals and inbox triage requiring a person, the oldest age and visible page count, plus server-side totals. Reports and check findings are excluded. Overview first, then `wikikit_health` on the space that needs attention | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_outputs` | knowledge:read | What the wiki produced: past grounded answers plus scheduled briefings and health reports; omit `output_id` to list (`kind` narrows), pass it to read one whole. NOT knowledge — derived artifacts | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_promote_output` | knowledge:propose | Propose an answer as knowledge by filing it as a source marked derived from the wiki itself; briefing/health reports are rejected. Runs the ORDINARY pipeline (dedup, grounding guard, contradiction detection) and ends in one proposal a HUMAN approves → `{status:"running", ingest_id, poll_with:"wikikit_ingest_status"}` | false | true | true | false |
| `wikikit_charter` | knowledge:read | Read the space charter — virtual document (authored steering markdown + derived KB overview); `rev` for a version | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_charter_history` | knowledge:read | List charter revisions (newest first) — the document version history | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_charter_set` | admin | Write the charter: authored text versions directly, an edited overview routes through the review gate → `{rev, ingest_ids}` | false | true | false | false |
| `wikikit_charter_delete` | admin | Supersede the current charter revision (history retained); idempotent | false | true | true | false |
| `wikikit_deleted_concepts` | knowledge:read | List deleted concept tombstones | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_concept_delete` | knowledge:propose | Stage page deletion for review | false | true | true | false |
| `wikikit_concept_restore` | knowledge:propose | Stage page restoration for review | false | true | true | false |
| `wikikit_ingest` | knowledge:propose | Submit a source → async ack `{status:"running", ingest_id, poll_with:"wikikit_ingest_status"}`; `capture:true` parks it keyless → `{status:"captured", ingest_id}` (triage is a human step in the Cockpit) | false | true | true | true |
| `wikikit_ingest_status` | knowledge:propose | Poll an ingest job; terminal: done (proposal_id) / failed (error) / discarded; captured = parked for a human | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_propose` | knowledge:propose | Stage a structured ChangeProposal → `{proposal_id, status:"pending"}` | false | true | true | false |
| `wikikit_proposals` | knowledge:review | List proposals or inspect one complete structured diff | true | false | true | false |
| `wikikit_review_proposal` | knowledge:review | Input `{proposal_id}` only; the human owns the decision — native form first (the in-client dialog); URL-mode fallback when the form is unavailable or unrendered (`url_review_started`, decision on the review page, completion notification); accepted review writes, decline/cancel are no-ops; no elicitation capability → `human_review_required` hand-off with `review_url`; `decision`/`note` as input → `approval_requires_human` | false | true | false | false |

Annotation rationale (fixed): writes are `destructiveHint: true` even though
they only stage content — an honest write is a write. `idempotentHint: true`
on the writes because content-hash dedup (ingest) and the pending input-hash
unique index (propose) make identical retries converge. `openWorldHint: true`
only on `wikikit_ingest` (a `url` input fetches an external host);
`wikikit_promote_output` is the contrast — it writes and creates review work,
but the markdown is already in the database, so no host is contacted.

Do not promote routinely or in bulk: every promotion creates review work, and
an answer that only cites the wiki adds no outside evidence (the
`self-derived-only` lint rule reports pages that end up resting on nothing
else). There are deliberately no schedule tools — recurring maintenance is
installation configuration, driven over `PUT /v1/spaces/{space}/schedules` with
an `admin` credential, exactly as api-keys, webhooks and space administration
are. MCP hosts cache the scanned tool contract: after a release that adds tools,
rescan or reconnect.

Connect any MCP host over Streamable HTTP at `https://<host>/mcp`, using OAuth
or a narrow Bearer `wk_` key with the required knowledge scopes.

The native form is the primary review channel. For Codex, set
`approval_policy = { granular = { mcp_elicitations = true } }` and
`approvals_reviewer = "user"`. Claude Code requires 2.1.76 or newer. ChatGPT
review support is conditional on the active connector advertising native form
elicitation; reconnect and run a canary after deployment. A client advertising
`elicitation.url` gains the browser fallback for exactly the cases where the
form is unavailable or unrendered. Without any elicitation capability the
review hands off (`human_review_required` with a `review_url`): the human
opens the review page and decides there as themselves, and the agent reports
the outcome from `wikikit_proposals`.

---

## 8. Webhooks (Standard Webhooks)

State changes write a transactional outbox row; a delivery worker fans out to
matching endpoints with exponential backoff (up to
`WIKIKIT_WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS`) and a circuit breaker
(`WIKIKIT_WEBHOOK_CIRCUIT_THRESHOLD` consecutive failures → endpoint paused
15 min). Endpoint secrets are `whsec_`-style, shown once at registration.

Events:

```
wikikit.proposal.created    {proposal_id, space, title, source_ids, concepts, claims_count, contradictions_count, relations_removed_count}
wikikit.proposal.approved   {proposal_id, space, reviewer, note, review_channel, concepts}
wikikit.proposal.rejected   {proposal_id, space, reviewer, note, review_channel}
wikikit.concept.updated     {space, slug, rev, proposal_id}
wikikit.ingest.failed       {ingest_id, space, error: {code, message}}
wikikit.health.reported     {space, output_id, findings: {error, warn, info}, pending_proposals, oldest_pending_days}
```

`wikikit.health.reported` fires when a scheduled health run commits — the output
row and the event are written in one transaction, so no consumer is told about a
report that is not there to read. It carries the summary an alerting rule
branches on and not the report itself, which is behind `output_id`.
`oldest_pending_days` is null exactly when `pending_proposals` is 0.
**WikiKit sends no e-mail** — there is no SMTP in a single binary — so delivery
of a briefing or a health report is the output plus this webhook.

Envelope: HTTP POST `application/json` with Standard Webhooks headers —
`webhook-id` (`evt_<n>`), `webhook-timestamp` (unix seconds),
`webhook-signature` (`v1,<base64(hmacSHA256(secret, "{id}.{timestamp}.{body}"))>`).
Body: `{"type": "...", "timestamp": "<ISO 8601>", "data": {...}}`. Always
verify the signature (constant-time; the header may carry several
space-separated signatures during secret rotation). This is the standard seam
any system (n8n, a governance layer, anything) reacts through — no code
dependency.

---

## 9. Export / import (Markdown & OKF)

`GET /v1/spaces/{space}/export?format=md|okf` streams a zip; identical
knowledge always zips to identical bytes (deterministic snapshot + fixed file
order).

**Markdown tree** (`format=md`, Obsidian-friendly):

```
index.md               TOC with [[slug]] wiki links (derived, regenerated)
log.md                 audit narrative: proposal, reviewer, review channel, model (derived)
concepts/<slug>.md     claims + relations in YAML frontmatter, body = markdown
decisions/<slug>.md    context/decision/rationale/alternatives in frontmatter
sources/<hash>.md      kind/url/title in frontmatter, body = raw verbatim
```

Claims round-trip losslessly through frontmatter (see
`examples/concept-frontmatter-reference.md`). Citations reference sources by
content hash — ids never travel across systems.

**OKF bundle** (`format=okf`): conforms to the vendored Open Knowledge Format
v0.1 spec (`docs/okf-v0.1.md`); every manifest carries `okf_version: "0.1"`
plus a generator stamp. WikiKit-specific structure (claims, relations) rides
an extension block, so foreign OKF consumers still read the documents.

**Import** (`POST /v1/spaces/{space}/import?format=md|okf`, body = zip):
sources are archived directly; concepts/claims/decisions are staged as **one
ChangeProposal** — foreign knowledge passes the same review gate as LLM
output. Claim/decision status is re-derived by the gate on approve; review
history does not travel.

---

## 10. Knowledge lint

`GET /v1/spaces/{space}/lint` — LLM-free SQL checks, CI-consumable
(`{findings: [{rule, severity, message, concept_slug?, claim_id?, details?}], counts}`).
Each rule also carries a fixed tier: `?tier=quick` runs only the
queue/inbox/charter pulse rules, the default `deep` runs everything — deep is a
strict superset of quick, so the rhythms nest instead of forking.

| Rule | Severity | Tier |
|------|----------|------|
| `contradictions` | error | deep |
| `missing-citations` | error | deep |
| `broken-relations` | error | deep |
| `stale-claims` | warn | deep |
| `orphan-concepts` | warn | deep |
| `unsourced-concepts` | warn | deep |
| `self-derived-only` | warn | deep |
| `stub-concepts` | warn | deep |
| `scaffolded-claims` | warn | deep |
| `tombstoned-sources` | warn | deep |
| `broken-cross-space-links` | warn | deep |
| `stale-proposals` | warn | quick |
| `stale-captures` | warn | quick |
| `empty-concepts` | info | deep |
| `unreviewed-proposals` | info | quick |
| `dangling-sources` | info | quick |
| `missing-charter` | info | quick |

`stale-proposals` flags pending changes older than 14 days, with
`details: {proposal_id, title, days_open}` — the age is what turns a queue into
a backlog. `unreviewed-proposals` stays as the census of everything waiting;
the two deliberately overlap and a surface listing both should group them.
`stale-captures` flags thoughts parked longer than 30 days: an old inbox item
is a signal, not an error — capture bypasses every gate on purpose, and this
rule is the pressure valve. `missing-charter` (info) fires when the space has
no current charter revision, so the absence of a steering document is a visible
choice rather than an accident.

`unsourced-concepts` is the page-level evidence rule: a readable page across
whose visible claims there is not one citation — no archived document stands
behind it. It is a warn and not an error because a hand-written page is a
legitimate thing to have, and the finding names the fix (ingest a source and let
synthesis quote it). A page with no claims at all is reported by both this rule
and `empty-concepts`; `counts` is a census of findings, not of pages.

`self-derived-only` is the provenance rule, and the counterweight to promoting
answers back into the wiki: a readable page whose visible claims quote at least
one source marked `derived_from_output_id` and no source without one — knowledge
with no evidence from outside the wiki. Every neighbouring rule is correctly
silent about such a page (the sources exist, are archived verbatim, and are
quoted with real quotes); they all ask whether evidence is present, and this is
the one that asks where it came from. The review gate cannot see it either, since
each individual promotion looked right to the reviewer who approved it and only
the state at the end of the chain is circular. Warn, not error: a page resting on
a promoted answer is legitimate, and the finding disappears the moment one claim
cites one outside source. Its message names the fix as ingesting a source from
OUTSIDE the wiki — deliberately not what `unsourced-concepts` says, because an
operator reading "ingest a source" here would reasonably promote another answer,
which is the state rather than the cure.

The composed read `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/health` (and `wikikit_health`) serves
this whole report unchanged, plus the coverage block and the two live queues —
changes waiting for a human with the age of the oldest, and ingest work still in
flight, with the parked thoughts counted beside the queue (`captured`,
`oldest_captured_days` — null when nothing is parked). Beside those queues it
reports `archive` — `{sources, indexed, unindexed, index_days}`, the archive
against the retrieval index, published whether or not a window is set so the
size of the decision is visible before it is made; `index_days` is null when
sources stay indexed forever. It accepts the same
`tier` and is the same `lintSpace()` call, never a second count, so the two
surfaces cannot disagree about one space. Scheduled health runs always pass
tier deep: the persisted report is the full protocol.

`stub-concepts` is the page-level emptiness rule: a readable page with no body
text, no visible claims, and no active relation in either direction — titled, in
the index, openable, and blank. Every condition is an observable property of the
page rather than a marker on the revision that created it, so the rule reports
the same pages on every installation and does not depend on any one deployment's
import history. Unlike the other page-level rules it neither excludes nor
requires structural-scaffolding revisions: a scaffolding page nothing points
through any more is just a blank page. The fix it names is delete-or-write, not
ingest-a-source, which is why this is its own rule and not a relaxation of
`unsourced-concepts`.

`scaffolded-claims` is the contradiction rule, and the only page-level rule that
REQUIRES a scaffolding marker rather than excluding it: a readable page marked
as a reference target that nevertheless states visible claims. The marker
decides whether a page is a reference target and the counts are never consulted,
so such a page has its `evidence` withheld from the concept list and from
`kind: "concept"` search hits while its claims stay fully readable on the page.
Those two surfaces now say that a count is being withheld — `not_measured.
withheld_claims`, the same number from the same aggregate — and this rule is
what says it is a contradiction somebody should resolve, because no other
surface passes judgement on it. Warn, not error: the
claims are real and nothing in the knowledge is broken; what is broken is the
index's account of the page. The finding names the slug, the visible-claim
count, and both readings of the contradiction (the marker is wrong for this
page, or the claims belong on the page it points at) because the linter cannot
know which; it never names the marker itself. Pages carrying WikiKit's own
`structural-reference` are reported too — a claim on a page the product created
as structure is the more alarming case, not the exempt one.

---

## 11. Configuration (environment variables)

All config is via env vars (`WIKIKIT_*` prefix; optional `.env`; committed
`.env.defaults` supplies dev values and is **never** read when
`NODE_ENV=production`). Precedence: process env > `.env` > `.env.defaults`.
Invalid values fail the boot, not the request.

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `HOST` | bind address | `127.0.0.1` |
| `PORT` | HTTP listen port | `4060` |
| `WIKIKIT_PUBLIC_URL` | canonical OAuth issuer/resource + MCP origin allowlist; HTTPS in production | `http://127.0.0.1:4060` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Postgres connection string; **required in production** | dev: local Docker Postgres |
| `WIKIKIT_KEY_PEPPER` | HMAC pepper for API-key hashes; **required in production** | dev: committed dev pepper |
| `WIKIKIT_BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY` | pin the bootstrap admin key | (dev: generated + printed once) |
| `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT` | deployment identity in structured logs | `development` outside production |
| `WIKIKIT_LLM_PROVIDER` | LLM provider the AI SDK routes to: `anthropic`/`openai`/`google` | `anthropic` |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | key for the `anthropic` provider; enables ingest/query | (unset → 503 `llm_not_configured`) |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | key for the `openai` provider | (unset) |
| `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` | key for the `google` provider | (unset) |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | Anthropic API base (test stubs); honored when provider is `anthropic` | (empty) |
| `WIKIKIT_MODEL_SYNTHESIS` | synthesis model; default is an Anthropic id — set per provider, a foreign id fails the boot | `claude-sonnet-5` |
| `WIKIKIT_MODEL_CLASSIFY` | cheap/filter model: classification + session distillation; set per provider, a foreign id fails the boot | `claude-haiku-4-5` |
| `WIKIKIT_MODEL_ANSWER` | grounded-answer model; default is an Anthropic id — set per provider, a foreign id fails the boot | `claude-sonnet-5` |
| `WIKIKIT_MODEL_PRICES` | strict JSON model → `{input,output,cache_read}` USD per million measured tokens; no guessed prices | `{}` |
| `WIKIKIT_ANSWER_TOKEN_BUDGET` | estimated evidence-token ceiling for one grounded answer (1000–200000); truncation is reported | `36000` |
| `WIKIKIT_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` | optional hybrid-retrieval embedding provider: `none`/`openai`/`google`; also needs pgvector installed on the database host as an OS package | `none` (lexical-only) |
| `WIKIKIT_MODEL_EMBEDDING` | embedding model (must produce 1536-dim vectors); checked against `WIKIKIT_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` at boot unless that is `none` | `text-embedding-3-small` |
| `WIKIKIT_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | max request body → 413 | `10485760` (10 MiB) |
| `WIKIKIT_MAX_INGEST_TOKENS` | chunking threshold for large sources | `100000` |
| `WIKIKIT_INGEST_CONCURRENCY` | parallel ingest workers (1–16) | `2` |
| `WIKIKIT_INGEST_LEASE_MS` | worker lease before `worker_lost` reaping | `900000` |
| `WIKIKIT_INGEST_HEARTBEAT_MS` | lease renewal cadence (< half the lease) | `30000` |
| `WIKIKIT_INGEST_MAX_RUNTIME_MS` | wall-clock ceiling per job; over it → failed with `timeout` | `5400000` |
| `WIKIKIT_INGEST_MAX_QUEUED_PER_SPACE` | waiting jobs (`queued` + `quota_blocked`) per space before enqueue answers 429 `ingest_queue_full` | `200` |
| `WIKIKIT_OUTPUT_RETENTION_DAYS` | how long an UNPROMOTED output is kept (hourly sweep); `0` keeps forever, a promoted output is never collected | `365` |
| `WIKIKIT_SOURCE_INDEX_DAYS` | how long an archived source stays in the retrieval index (hourly sweep drops `wk_source_chunks`, never `wk_sources`); a cited source, one named by a pending/approved proposal, a stream head, one with an unfinished ingest job or one derived from an output is never unindexed; re-indexing is possible at any time | `0` (indexed forever) |
| `WIKIKIT_SCHEDULER_ENABLED` | run the in-process briefing/health worker; off leaves schedules saved and armed | `true` |
| `WIKIKIT_DEFAULT_BRIEFING` | the briefing a newly created wiki is armed with — `HH:MM`, `HH:MM <IANA zone>`, or `off`; a malformed value refuses to boot | `07:00` (UTC) |
| `WIKIKIT_WEBHOOK_POLL_MS` | outbox poll interval | `5000` (dev file: `1000`) |
| `WIKIKIT_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` | per-delivery HTTP timeout | `10000` |
| `WIKIKIT_WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | retries before a delivery is dead | `10` |
| `WIKIKIT_WEBHOOK_CIRCUIT_THRESHOLD` | consecutive failures → endpoint paused 15 min | `5` |
| `WIKIKIT_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE` | allow private/loopback webhook targets (SSRF guard) | `true` outside production |
| `WIKIKIT_TRUST_PROXY` | trust `X-Forwarded-*` (behind Caddy/nginx) | `false` |
| `WIKIKIT_MCP_SESSION_TTL_MS` | MCP idle session TTL | `1800000` (30 min) |
| `WIKIKIT_MCP_MAX_SESSIONS` | MCP session hard cap (oldest-idle eviction) | `200` |
| `WIKIKIT_MCP_ELICITATION_TIMEOUT_MS` | native human review-form timeout; fails closed (10 s–30 min) | `300000` (5 min) |
| `WIKIKIT_USAGE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` | enable privacy-bounded usage collection | `false` |
| `WIKIKIT_USAGE_HMAC_SECRET` | independent product-local HMAC secret; required when enabled | (unset) |
| `WIKIKIT_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` | raw usage retention (31–365 days) | `90` |
| `WIKIKIT_COVERAGE_GAP_TOPICS_ENABLED` | opt-in: store stemmed lexemes (never text) of unanswered queries | `false` |
| `WIKIKIT_SCAFFOLDING_KINDS` | extra revision kinds marking a page as structure, not knowledge (evidence reported absent, not zero); `structural-reference` is always built in | (unset) |
| `WIKIKIT_OAUTH_DCR_ENABLED` | RFC 7591 dynamic registration for remote MCP clients | `true` |
| `WIKIKIT_OAUTH_CODE_TTL_MS` | authorization-code TTL | `600000` (10 min) |
| `WIKIKIT_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MS` | access-token TTL | `3600000` (1 h) |
| `WIKIKIT_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_MS` | rotating refresh-token TTL | `2592000000` (30 d) |
| `WIKIKIT_OAUTH_OPERATOR_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TTL_MS` | absolute ceiling on a browser operator session, stamped at mint; renewal never passes it (8 h–30 d, floor is the 8 h idle window) | `86400000` (24 h) |
| `WIKIKIT_OAUTH_ALLOWED_SCOPES` | interactive identity permission ceiling | `knowledge:read,knowledge:propose` |
| `WIKIKIT_OAUTH_ENABLE_SIGNUP` | auto-admit unknown OIDC identities at the SSO callback with the minimal `knowledge:read` ceiling | `false` |
| `WIKIKIT_OAUTH_PROVIDERS` | WikiKit-local browser-provider configuration; JSON records use `protocol: api_key` or `oidc` | API-key record |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `debug`/`info`/`warn`/`error` | `info` |
| `NODE_ENV` | `production` activates guards + disables `.env.defaults` | (unset) |

Zero-config principle: `./wikikit` with nothing configured boots a complete
local stack — Docker Postgres is provisioned automatically, migrations run
under an advisory lock, a default space is created, and a bootstrap key is
printed once. Only the provider API keys (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`) have no default, and only the
one matching `WIKIKIT_LLM_PROVIDER` is read; without it every LLM-free feature
still works. In production the behavior flips: no
auto-provisioning, `DATABASE_URL` and `WIKIKIT_KEY_PEPPER` are mandatory.

`WIKIKIT_OAUTH_PROVIDERS` is a JSON array with unique `id`, `protocol`, and
`label`. API-key records select a product-local key policy; direct OIDC records
add HTTPS `issuer_url`, `client_id`, optional `client_secret`,
`scopes` (including `openid`), `allowed_subjects` and/or `allowed_emails`, and
optional identity-policy overrides. At least one subject or email entry is
required; subject matching is exact and email matching requires
`email_verified=true`. Register
`${WIKIKIT_PUBLIC_URL}/v1/identity/login/callback` with each OIDC provider. Keep
client secrets in the production secret store, never in the repository.

---

## 12. Running & deploying

- **Dev:** `bun run dev` (Bun runs TypeScript natively; no build step).
- **Single binary:** `bun run build:binary` → `dist/wikikit` (a true
  `bun build --compile` executable; no unpack step, no Node on the host).
  Ops flags only — this is not a CLI product: no args starts the server,
  `--migrate` migrates and exits, `--version` prints the version.
- **Self-migrating boot:** every start (and `--migrate`) applies the embedded
  SQL migrations under a Postgres advisory lock before HTTP opens; a migration
  failure keeps `/ready` down so the deploy health gate rolls back. A recorded
  tag is never re-executed, so a guarded migration that skipped its body (0018,
  behind pgvector) stays skipped forever — installing pgvector afterwards needs
  the new tag 0041, which creates what 0018 could not and no-ops everywhere
  else. Boot reports `vector_available` and warns when an embedding provider is
  configured without the extension; neither gates startup.
- **Cockpit:** the one human interface, served by this same process at
  `/cockpit` and built into the same artifact — a space reads as a wiki, a
  concept as a Markdown page, and an edit becomes a change proposal somebody
  has to approve. `bun run dev:cockpit` runs it against a local API on :4060;
  `bun run build:cockpit` regenerates `assets/cockpit` and
  `src/cockpit-embedded.ts`, both committed and both drift-gated by
  `bun run check:cockpit-drift`. Its credential plane is §3; the design
  contract it implements is `contract/COCKPIT-UI.md`. Full notes:
  [docs/COCKPIT.md](docs/COCKPIT.md).

Lifecycle: `/health` (liveness), `/ready` (readiness — `{status, version}`;
deploy gates match **both** fields; 503 while draining). On SIGTERM/SIGINT the
service fails `/ready`, stops the workers, drains in-flight requests, then
exits 0. A draining instance keeps serving the probes, the `/cockpit` bundle
and the human sign-in funnel, and refuses everything else: REST routes and the
OAuth machine plane (discovery, registration, token mint and revocation) with
`503 {"code":"draining"}`, and `/mcp` with a 503 carrying a JSON-RPC error
frame — re-run `initialize` against another instance. Logs are structured JSON on stdout with request ids; API keys are
never logged.

**Checks:** `bun run gate` runs everything CI runs (~60s, needs Docker) and
installs as a `pre-push` hook via `bun run hooks:install`. Five tiers, each
covering what the one below cannot: `test/unit` (logic + the drift gates that
keep these docs true), `test/contract` (snapshots foreign systems consume),
`test/integration` (real Postgres, FakeProvider), `test/e2e` (the REAL AI SDK
against a stub Anthropic endpoint — the only tier that sees the vendor edge:
request shape, `cache_control` placement, usage mapping), and `benchmarks/`
(`bun run bench` — reports, never gates; the cost regression that does gate is
`test/unit/prompt-budget.test.ts`).

---

## 13. Integration (standards only)

WikiKit integrates **only over open standards** (OpenAPI/REST, MCP, Standard
Webhooks, OKF, llms.txt) — no SDK, no shared code, no direct dependencies. Any
external system consumes it the same way:

- **OpenAPI/REST** — `/openapi.json` is a ready-to-import connector for the full API.
- **MCP** — federate `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) to give an agent search/read/propose and permission-gated review tools.
- **Standard Webhooks** — subscribe to `wikikit.proposal.created`, `proposal.approved`, `concept.updated`, `ingest.failed`.
- **OKF / Markdown tree** — portable knowledge import and export.

Typical seams: a governance layer imports the OpenAPI connector or federates
the MCP server and reacts to `wikikit.proposal.created` with an approval
workflow; a publishing pipeline reads an approved concept and posts a curated
projection out as an article; that published article is re-ingested by URL and
becomes a citable source.

---

## 14. Troubleshooting

- **401 unauthorized** — key missing/revoked or the server's
  `WIKIKIT_KEY_PEPPER` changed (hashes no longer match).
- **403 insufficient_scope** — key lacks the scope, or a space-scoped key
  touched a foreign space.
- **409 already_ingested** — the exact content was ingested before; the
  envelope carries the existing `source_id`. Not an error for retries — the
  pipeline is idempotent by design.
- **409 stale_base on approve** — the concept changed since the proposal was
  created; re-ingest or re-propose against the current revision.
- **429 ingest_queue_full** — this space already has
  `WIKIKIT_INGEST_MAX_QUEUED_PER_SPACE` jobs waiting and nothing was queued. Do
  not retry in a loop: check `GET /v1/spaces/{space}/ingests?status=queued` and
  clear the pending proposals the earlier jobs produced. A full queue usually
  means the review gate, not the worker, is the bottleneck.
- **503 llm_not_configured** — set the key the error names (the one for the
  configured `WIKIKIT_LLM_PROVIDER`); all LLM-free routes
  keep working meanwhile.
- **Webhook endpoint stopped receiving** — check
  `GET .../webhooks/{id}/deliveries` (newest first; `?limit=` up to 200,
  default 50, no cursor — a full answer is a truncated one); after repeated
  failures the circuit breaker pauses the endpoint for 15 minutes.
- **MCP client loops on session errors** — re-initialize on JSON-RPC `-32001`;
  sessions expire after `WIKIKIT_MCP_SESSION_TTL_MS` idle.
- **MCP review returns `human_review_required`** — the client cannot show the
  native review form. The proposal stays pending; the agent gives the user
  the returned `review_url` (the `GET /review/{id}` page) where the human
  decides as themselves; the agent polls `wikikit_proposals`. Never approve
  via chat, tool arguments, or REST calls made on the human's behalf.
- **MCP review returns `approval_requires_human`** — the agent passed
  `decision`/`note` as tool input. The tool takes only `proposal_id`; WikiKit
  collects the decision from the human, never from the agent.
